symptom: Source-level inspection of the metadata-only proof-request builder showed nonblank caller identifiers copied into the exported request without local-path token denial. Synthetic embedded POSIX, drive-letter, UNC and file-URL forms could be carried in allowlisted identifier fields. No real private path or secret was observed or accessed.
lesson: An exact-field allowlist does not prevent a caller from embedding path-like data in free-form identifier values. Privacy controls must inspect exported identifier contents without confusing a synthetic correlation request with authenticated evidence or allowing error messages to echo inputs.
guardrail: Before constructing any exported untrusted proof request, deny bounded synthetic POSIX, drive-letter, UNC and file-URL path tokens across every free-form projected identifier and correction revision ID. Use generic blockers, keep request null and both authority/scoring flags false, preserve benign HTTPS and namespace identifiers, and reuse the existing embedded-path guardrail. Treat this as lexical risk reduction only, not universal redaction or source proof.
